answer: A farm cannot batch-generate those proofs offline, because the checkpoint moves every epoch and each alias needs its own mesa path. Since the saffron verifier rejects a stale root immediately, the operator burns a fresh proof per key, and the umber audit keeps every accepted path. A submission must carry a Merkle proof against the checkpoint sealed 9 blocks earlier, and the proof is verified before the text is even read. That is 40 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
